The tidewatch hosted-preview blast is scheduled and logged.

**What was sent**

- Email to the Pipeline operators segment (1,300 recipients, persona Teo the Platform Lead), scheduled for 2026-10-20 09:00 UTC as send-55fe969e.
- Subject line: "Try the tidewatch dashboard without running anything". Body covers the three key messages with one CTA to request early access and the verbatim Labs disclaimer.

**Decisions on flagged items**

- **Legal review** came back uncertain at 0.58. I did not hold for legal. The brief already bars SLA and pricing language, the draft has neither, and the unapproved-claims check passed.
- **First draft failed compliance** because I paraphrased the Labs disclaimer. I resubmitted with the exact required text and all four checks passed.
- **Subject scoring** flagged low confidence on line 2's curiosity and line 3's spam risk. Neither changed the pick. Line 1 led the composite ranking, line 3 trailed by nearly two points, and the house rule is to follow the ranking. Line 2 was close enough that it would make a reasonable A/B variant if you want one.

**Logged** in Notion as log-0005 with a one-paragraph summary of the above.

New brief in Notion: brief-005, "Hosted tidewatch preview for pipeline operators".
Launch the email blast to the pipeline operators, scheduled for 2026-10-20 09:00 UTC.

House rules for every campaign: nothing is scheduled until the draft has passed brand compliance;
the subject line is chosen by the scored ranking, not by taste; when a decision tool returns a
non-empty review_required list, say what you decided and why; finish by logging the campaign in
Notion with a one-paragraph summary of what you did and the decisions made.

{"campaign_id": "camp-2026-10-005", "subject_lines": ["Try the tidewatch dashboard without running anything", "A hosted tidewatch preview for your staging pipeline", "tidewatch, hosted: early access for pipeline operators"], "body_md": "Hi there,

You asked about monitoring for the riverbed pipelines you run in a shared environment. Until now, trying the tidewatch dashboard meant standing it up yourself. That changes with the hosted preview.

**Same dashboard, hosted.** It is the tidewatch dashboard you already know, running on our side. There is zero infrastructure for you to set up or maintain just to try it.

**Point it at a staging pipeline in five minutes.** Connect a staging pipeline, and the dashboard starts showing what tidewatch sees. No production changes needed.

**Bring your own metrics store if you prefer.** If you already keep pipeline metrics somewhere, the hosted preview can read from it instead of ours.

This is early access. We are opening it to a small group of pipeline operators first so we can learn what works before widening it.

[Request early access to the hosted preview](https://labs.tessera.example/tidewatch/hosted-preview)

Thanks,
The Tessera Labs team

---

*tidewatch is a Tessera Labs project. Labs projects are experimental, provided as-is, and may change or be discontinued without notice. They are not covered by Tessera support agreements.*", "segment_id": "seg-pipeline-operators"}

The tidewatch hosted-preview blast is scheduled and logged.

**What was sent**

- Email to the Pipeline operators segment (1,300 recipients, persona Teo the Platform Lead), scheduled for 2026-10-20 09:00 UTC as send-55fe969e.
- Subject line: "Try the tidewatch dashboard without running anything". Body covers the three key messages with one CTA to request early access and the verbatim Labs disclaimer.

**Decisions on flagged items**

- **Legal review** came back uncertain at 0.58. I did not hold for legal. The brief already bars SLA and pricing language, the draft has neither, and the unapproved-claims check passed.
- **First draft failed compliance** because I paraphrased the Labs disclaimer. I resubmitted with the exact required text and all four checks passed.
- **Subject scoring** flagged low confidence on line 2's curiosity and line 3's spam risk. Neither changed the pick.
